<!-- Use a topic-level title: Development:, Design:, Fix:, Audit:, Docs:, CI:, or Research:.
Every PR, including a small fix, must complete the six sections below.
Keep this description current; put chronological checkpoints in comments or durable docs.
When opening through an API or connector, supply this template explicitly.
Before publication, apply docs/PUBLICATION_PREFLIGHT.md to descriptions, comments, logs, screenshots and attachments; withhold sensitive or uncleared material.
Replace prompts; use "None" or "Not applicable — reason" when appropriate. -->

## Overview
<!-- In plain language: what problem or opportunity, why this matters, and the intended result. -->

## Scope and changes
<!-- What changes, affected components/documents, and important exclusions or compatibility effects. -->

## Status and progress
<!-- Draft / in development / under review / ready for owner disposition / closed outcome.
For a multi-stage topic, include a compact milestone table. Separate design, implemented source and acceptance. -->

## Verification
<!-- Exact candidate revision and links to named executed checks/results. Distinguish pending, failed, blocked, not run and not applicable. Explain evidence limits, including actual target validation when relevant. -->

## Limitations and next steps
<!-- Remaining defects, provisional decisions, deferred work, dependencies, and the next concrete action. State explicitly if none are known. -->

## References and integration
<!-- Links to relevant requirements, source/docs, issues/PRs, evidence and review disposition.
Record the integration outcome at closeout; never infer merge authorization. -->

<!-- Optional for substantial work: Visual preview (publication-cleared images), alternatives and rationale,
migration/rollback, milestone breakdown, performance, audit table, or additional review context.
See docs/development/PR_DOCUMENTATION_STANDARD.md for guidance. -->
